findings.title: Async gjs module failure may exit 0 and pass CTest
findings.why_it_matters: CTest judges this test only by gjs's exit code. Because the fixture uses top-level await, it is an async module. Every assertion from line 76 onward, plus the ARGV and file-load throws at lines 26-29, settles the module-evaluation promise as a rejection. Node exited 1 on a rejected top-level await and exited 13 on a top-level await that never settled. I could not confirm that every distro gjs that `find_program` might find does the same. On some versions a rejection may only be logged as an unhandled rejection. A promise that never settles may let the job queue drain and exit 0. Either way the five ownership assertions could report green while one of them is red.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop relying on gjs's exit-code semantics. Add `PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PASS helper registration/focus changes do not replace frozen target"` to the existing `set_tests_properties(gnome_ui_ownership_contract PROPERTIES TIMEOUT 30)`. The last PASS line prints only after every earlier assertion and await has finished in order. Belt-and-braces option: wrap the test body in `try { ... } catch (e) { logError(e); System.exit(1); }` using `import System from 'system'` (built into GJS, not a new dependency).
evidence: CMakeLists.txt:375-376: `add_test(NAME gnome_ui_ownership_contract COMMAND "${PUTGD_GJS}" -m ".../test_gnome_ownership.mjs" ".../extension.js")` / `set_tests_properties(gnome_ui_ownership_contract PROPERTIES TIMEOUT 30)`: no PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION or FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, so the verdict is the exit code alone.

tests/desktop/test_gnome_ownership.mjs:76: `await assert.rejects(own.extension._prepare(...), e => e.bridgeCode === 'capture_target');` is the first top-level await. From here every `assert.*` throw rejects the async module-evaluation promise; it is not a synchronous script exception.

Never-settled scenario: `register()` (lines 65-69) resolves only through the mocked `return_value`. Suppose the extension answers an error path through an unmocked invocation method such as `return_dbus_error`. The resulting TypeError is swallowed inside the async D-Bus handler and the promise never settles. Node would have exited 13. gjs either hangs until the 30 s TIMEOUT (red) or ends with the evaluation still pending (possibly exit 0 = green).

Lines 102-106: if `_prepare` fails before `_layout` is called, `releaseLayout` is undefined and `releaseLayout([])` throws after several awaits. That is again a failure that depends on async-module rejection handling.
findings.first_evidence: CMakeLists.txt:375-376: `add_test(NAME gnome_ui_ownership_contract COMMAND "${PUTGD_GJS}" -m ".../test_gnome_ownership.mjs" ".../extension.js")` / `set_tests_properties(gnome_ui_ownership_contract PROPERTIES TIMEOUT 30)`: no PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION or FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, so the verdict is the exit code alone.

findings.title: Missing gjs silently removes the ownership contract from ctest
findings.why_it_matters: Before this change, a machine without Node got a CMake WARNING. Now a machine without gjs registers no test and prints only a STATUS line, which is lost in normal configure output. On any build or CI host that had node but has no gjs, the five helper/resident ownership assertions drop out of `ctest`. The results show no Not Run, Skipped or Failed entry, so the suite looks fully green with the ownership-exclusion coverage gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the gap visible without adding a dependency. In the `else()` branch, register `add_test(NAME gnome_ui_ownership_contract COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E false)` with `set_tests_properties(gnome_ui_ownership_contract PROPERTIES DISABLED TRUE)` so ctest reports it as 'Not Run (Disabled)'. Keep `message(WARNING ...)` instead of STATUS. Optionally add a cache option, such as PUTGD_REQUIRE_GJS_CONTRACT, that turns a missing gjs into FATAL_ERROR in the GNOME lab.
evidence: CMakeLists.txt:378: `message(STATUS "GNOME extension ownership contract runs in the GNOME lab with its native GJS runtime")`

Diff removes `message(WARNING "Node.js unavailable: GNOME extension ownership fixture cannot run")`: the severity is downgraded at the same time the required runtime changes from node to gjs, which is much less common on generic build hosts.
CMakeLists.txt:374: `if(PUTGD_GJS)` is the only path that calls add_test, so the test name does not exist at all when gjs is absent.
findings.first_evidence: CMakeLists.txt:378: `message(STATUS "GNOME extension ownership contract runs in the GNOME lab with its native GJS runtime")`

residual_risks: Direct `eval(source)` (test_gnome_ownership.mjs:50) runs the extension in the whole module scope plus real GJS globals (`imports`, `console`, `log`, `setTimeout`, `ARGV`, `print`, `TextDecoder`, `FileIO`). The comment at line 48 says it captures 'only these deliberately mocked Shell dependencies', but that is not true. The old `vm.createContext` sandbox raised ReferenceError on any unmocked dependency. Now such a dependency silently uses the real GJS facility. For example, a real `setTimeout` scheduled on a main loop that never runs could hide a code path instead of failing the fixture.

`gjs -m` needs GJS ≥ 1.68, and `TextDecoder` with `{fatal: true}` needs a newer GJS still. If `find_program` finds an older distro gjs on a host build machine, the test is registered but fails with an interpreter/option error. That is a false red unrelated to the extension. It is not silent, but it could push people to delete or ignore the test.
testing_gaps: Nothing proves this gate turns red under gjs. No check deliberately breaks an assertion after the first top-level await (or leaves a `register()` promise pending) to confirm that `ctest` reports gnome_ui_ownership_contract as failed with the distro gjs the lab uses.
